answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a refundable deposit to earn a persistent reputation, like a ferrous anchor holding it in place. Misbehavior slashes the deposit, so a Sybil attacker faces a cost that scales linearly with every fake identity — a ripple of small deposits becomes a flood of locked capital. Reputation then accrues only through verified useful work over time, so a fresh identity starts on a low knoll with no trust, and climbing it takes sustained honest service that cannot be faked in bulk.
